title: Russia Resumes Mass Attacks as Truce Ends, Killing 5 and Injuring 70 Nationwide
detail: Russia ended its reciprocal 72-hour pause on strikes against Kyiv with a mass missile-and-drone assault in the early hours of September 8, killing at least 5 people and injuring around 70 nationwide, one day after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner concluded their shuttle diplomacy between Moscow and Kyiv. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 166 drones, 32 cruise missiles, and an unspecified number of anti-ship and ballistic missiles overnight; Ukrainian forces downed 142 drones, 31 cruise missiles, and two ballistic missiles. In Kyiv, at least 3 people were killed and 25 injured as strikes hit the Darnytskyi, Holosiivskyi, Podilskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, and Solomianskyi districts, damaging residential buildings, a school, and warehouses; drone wreckage struck a four-story office building in Solomianskyi around noon, sparking a fire and evacuations. President Zelensky said the barrage was designed to 'cause as much harm to life as possible.'

media.caption: Aftermath of Russia's mass missile and drone assault on Kyiv after the truce for US envoy visits expired, September 8, 2026

title: Trump Holds Hour-Long 'Frank' Call With Putin as Strikes Resume on Kyiv
detail: President Trump held an hour-long phone call with Vladimir Putin on September 8, the Kremlin said, following the weekend visits by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv. Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov described the call as 'constructive and quite candid,' saying Trump pressed for an early end to the war to open the way for 'impressive' US-Russia trade prospects, while Putin outlined his vision for the peace process, gave his assessment of the war, and assured Trump that Russia has 'no aggressive plans toward Europe.' The call came the same day Russia resumed mass strikes on Kyiv after the reciprocal 72-hour pause tied to the envoys' visit expired. Trump was expected to speak with Zelensky next.

media.caption: President Trump spoke with Vladimir Putin by phone for an hour on September 8, 2026, following the US envoys' Moscow and Kyiv visits
